papers.title: StateAct: Program State, before Pixels, for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  Computer-use agents are usually improved by strengthening perception: better models for reading a screenshot and choosing where to click. Yet a screenshot is only a lossy rendering of the underlying program state, e.g., the files, application backends, and DOM that hold the task data. Different states can produce the same pixels, while code can inspect and modify that state directly. StateAct is a code-first, multi-agent harness built around this distinction. Its main agent works directly with program state by using code, while a dedicated GUI subagent handles screenshot-and-click interaction on the few subgoals that need it, just 28 of 108 tasks and 1.1% of main-agent steps. The same direct access to program state also supports verification: an independent finish gate double-checks the saved result for structural failures, e.g., output that is missing, unsaved, or written to the wrong path. To stay on track over hundreds of steps, the main agent hands subgoals to fresh subagents, keeping its own context focused. On OSWorld 2.0, StateAct lifts Claude Opus 4.8 from 20.6% to 26.9% on binary success, and from 54.8% to 61.6% on partial success, at ~ 9x lower cost per task than the same model driven by screenshots alone; a code-only variant with no GUI subagent reaches only 45.9% partial, below that screenshot-based baseline's 54.8%. In general, grounding action, verification, and memory in state, what we call state-grounding, shifts the main bottleneck from perception toward reasoning: failures depend more on what the agent thinks than on what it sees.

ru.title: Переход от восприятия к мышлению
ru.desc: В данной статье представлена новая система StateAct, которая улучшает производительность агентов, работающих с компьютерными интерфейсами, благодаря прямому взаимодействию с состоянием программы. Вместо того чтобы полагаться только на скриншоты, основной агент использует код для доступа к данным, что позволяет избежать потерь информации и улучшить проверку результатов. Статья показывает, что такая реализация привела к значительному снижению затрат и повышению эффективности выполнения задач. Также подчеркивается, что успешность выполнения зависит больше от мышления агента, чем от его восприятия.

en.title: Revolutionizing Agent Performance with State-Grounded Reasoning
en.desc: This paper introduces StateAct, a multi-agent system that enhances computer-use agents by allowing them to interact directly with program state instead of relying solely on visual screenshots. By using a main agent that accesses the underlying code and a GUI subagent for limited visual tasks, the system improves efficiency and accuracy in task completion. StateAct also incorporates a verification mechanism to ensure the integrity of results, reducing errors related to output management. Overall, this approach shifts the focus from perception to reasoning, demonstrating that the agent's understanding of the state is crucial for success.

papers.title: DriveDNA: A Large-Scale Multimodal Naturalistic Driving Dataset and Benchmark for Driving Style Identification
papers.abstract: Abstract  Driving style captures stable, driver-specific patterns in how a vehicle is driven. In naturalistic data, however, this signal is hard to isolate because drivers are observed in different vehicles, on different roads, and under different conditions, so models may mistake vehicle- or situation-specific regularities for driver-specific style. We introduce DriveDNA, a large-scale naturalistic dataset and benchmark for personalized driving-style modeling, comprising 4,121 drives from 465 drivers across 115 vehicle models and totaling 975 hours of human-controlled driving at 10 Hz with forward video, collected from community drivers in everyday use. DriveDNA defines driving style as a consistent, driver-specific behavioral pattern in how a vehicle moves under similar conditions. The benchmark evaluates this signal through three core tasks: few-shot driver re-identification, personalized behavior prediction, and condition-matched comparison, and provides behavioral annotations plus 276,248 rule-generated maneuver events across six classes with large-scale human auditing. We evaluate baselines spanning classical descriptors, supervised and self-supervised time-series encoders, multimodal fusion, probabilistic prediction, and zero-shot foundation models under a fixed multi-seed protocol. Learned representations substantially outperform classical descriptors on unseen drivers (AUROC .935 vs. .707) and retain driver-specific information under matched driving conditions, while descriptor performance approaches chance. Video-only models achieve comparable re-identification accuracy but exhibit severe route leakage, showing that strong recognition may arise from contextual shortcuts rather than driving behavior. These findings show that reliable driving-style evaluation must assess both the behavioral value of learned representations and their robustness to vehicle, drive, and condition confounds.

ru.title: Новый взгляд на стиль вождения с DriveDNA
ru.desc: Статья представляет DriveDNA, новый набор данных и бенчмарк для моделирования стиля вождения, включающий 4,121 поездку от 465 водителей на 115 моделях автомобилей. Исследование подчеркивает трудности в выделении стиля вождения водителям из-за влияния различных условий. DriveDNA позволяет оценить стиль вождения через задачи, такие как повторная идентификация водителей и предсказание поведения. Результаты показывают, что обученные представления значительно превосходят традиционные дескрипторы в оценке стиля вождения.

en.title: DriveDNA: Unraveling Personalized Driving Styles
en.desc: This paper presents DriveDNA, a comprehensive dataset and benchmark designed to model personalized driving styles. It addresses the challenge of distinguishing driver-specific behaviors from vehicle and situational influences in naturalistic driving data. The benchmark includes tasks like few-shot driver re-identification and personalized behavior prediction, supported by extensive behavioral annotations. Results show that advanced learned representations significantly outperform traditional methods in recognizing driver-specific patterns while maintaining robustness against various driving conditions.
